title: ControlPlane hypothesis bench notes - April 28 2026
content:
Purpose: quick capture of ideas and small bench runs from the 4/28 controlplane sync. This is more of a lab notebook than a formal postmortem. Use it to seed follow-ups/tickets.

Summary / context:
- Focus areas from today's standup: routing fallthrough behavior, auth token cache churn, quota-bucket spike observed on canary.
- We ran 3 short micro-bench experiments on a local dev rig (2xA100-like VMs) to isolate cause of p95 latency spikes when route-fallthrough triggers fallback to cheaper model group.

Experiment A: KV-cache warm vs cold with frequent route changes
- Hypothesis: frequent route reassignment invalidates prefix entries in the in-memory controlplane KV cache, causing higher tail latencies due to rehydration overhead.
- Setup: replayed 10k synthetic requests (avg seq length 120 tokens) with route reassign every 200 requests. Measured controlplane RPC latency and downstream model-launch handshake time.
- Result: cold-warm delta ~18-22ms median on controlplane RPCs; p95 delta 45-70ms when reassign cadence <500 reqs. KV lookup hit-rate dropped from 98% -> 71%.
- Notes: reassigns were implemented via fake routing updates; stronger effect when updates were routed through the auth proxy layer.

Experiment B: Auth token cache TTL vs validation cost
- Hypothesis: overly short auth cache TTL combined with extra OIDC validation increases auth proxy CPU and adds queuing latency to route evaluation.
- Setup: rotated token TTL 3s / 10s / 30s under 2k rps steady load. Measured auth-proxy CPU, token validation calls to IDP, and added latency on route decision critical path.
- Result: 3s TTL caused 3x increase in IDP validation calls and auth-proxy CPU increased by ~60%. End-to-end p95 increased ~20ms. 30s TTL removed most extra overhead with negligible security tradeoff for internal service tokens.
- Action: propose adding per-client TTL override for internal infra tokens (ticket PLT-3499).

Experiment C: Quota bucket refill bath timing and burst coupling
- Hypothesis: simultaneous bucket refills across many tenants (clock alignment) explains observed short spike in request rejections and retry storms.
- Setup: simulated 500 tenants with aligned refill window vs jittered refill windows.
- Result: aligned refill produced a rejection spike (5s window) with concurrent retries producing request queueing; jittered refill flattened tail and reduced collision by ~82%.
- Quick fix: add randomized jitter to refill schedule in quota service; longer-term: explore distributed refill leaky-bucket model.

Open questions surfaced:
- Is KV cache sharding by route owner feasible within the current controlplane data model? Pros: smaller invalidation blast radius. Cons: requires migration for pinned variants and rollout logic. (Raised by Dmitri in standup).
- Can auth proxy expose a lightweight token introspection cache layer that can be warmed on controlplane route-change events? (Maya will prototype).
- How many customers rely on strict per-second refill alignment (edge cases for metered billing)? Need to ask CS before changing refill semantics.

Action items / owners (short list):
- PLT-3499 (Asha): add internal-token TTL override and integration test for auth-proxy; aim for PR by 2026-05-05.
- PLT-3421 (Dmitri): spike proposal for KV cache sharding + migration plan; initial design doc by 2026-05-07.
- Quota jitter patch (Jordan): small low-risk change to add +/- 500ms jitter to refill schedule; roll to canary, monitor for billing anomalies; PR target 2026-05-02.
- Bench harness (Maya): parameterize route-reassign cadence in replay tool, add metric export for KV hit-rate, PR to infra/bench repo.

Immediate follow-ups for next standup:
- Short demo of bench harness showing the 3 tests (5–10min).
- Decision call about auth TTL for infra tokens (need quick sign-off from security).
- Roll quota jitter to canary and monitor error/retry traces in Sentry and routing traces in Jaeger.

Notes to self (quick, informal):
- If we shard KV cache by route-owner, think about TTL/eviction policy per shard (hot tenants will need special handling).
- Watch out for extra coupling: route rollouts that change model variants might still require global canonicalization or a mapping layer — watch PR #789 for mapping util.
- Don't forget to link to the billing team before changing refill semantics.

Meeting log excerpt (raw):
- 09:05: Asha: "saw p95 spike on canary when fallback happened" -> quick triage -> hypothesis list (cache/auth/quota)
- 09:14: Jordan: "quota refill aligned across tenants, we saw retry storms"
- 09:22: Dmitri: "I can prototype sharded kv model but need migration safety"
- 09:30: Maya: "I can wire up bench harness to export kv-hit-rate and controlplane rpc timing"

Quick metrics snapshot from local bench (approx):
- baseline: controlplane RPC p50=6ms p95=18ms
- after reassign spike (Experiment A): p50=8ms p95=92ms
- auth short TTL (3s) p95 add = +20ms approx
- quota aligned refill spike: 5s window with error rate bump from 0.02% -> 1.4%

Draft decisions to record once approved:
- Add small refill jitter by default for quota buckets (opt-out via tenant flag).
- Allow internal infra tokens a longer TTL and an override mechanism.
- Signal to platform infra that KV-cache sharding spike will be a medium-sized project (design doc first).

Misc links and references (paste here so others can find):
- replay harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform-replay (bench branch: controlplane-kv-warm)
- related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/789
- confluence sketch: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLT/kv-cache-experiments

End notes: this doc is intentionally rough. If you want something moved into a formal RFC or Confluence page, flag it in the next standup or add a comment here.
